reasons: Deviation is real: Section 14.2 grants a revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence limited to the Order Form term and silent on Affiliates/contractors — squarely the walk-away position and inconsistent with Sections 13.2–13.3.

Redline reaches the preferred position: it names Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf, makes the licence perpetual/irrevocable and fully paid, adds transfer to an Affiliate or successor, and limits revocation/suspension to the Section 13.3 uncured-breach path; Vendor's ownership sentence is preserved so the edit is directionally correct and no broader than needed.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.811 changed-character ratio) is justified here: the offending grant sentence had to be replaced wholesale because every operative term (revocable, non-transferable, Order Form-term limit, missing Affiliates) conflicted with the rule; the first sentence was left intact.

Comment is accurate, uses the [Playbook] prefix, cites the internal inconsistency with Sections 13.2/13.3 as the basis, explains the harm in two sentences, and matches the required concise first-person-plural tone; 'high' severity is appropriate for a walk-away licence term.
